business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K business section and the Q3 2026 10-Q MD&A.
business_model.claim: RLJ is a hotel REIT that owns premium-branded, focused-service and compact full-service hotels in urban markets. It owned 92 hotels with about 20,600 rooms at September 30, 2026.
quotes: owns primarily premium-branded, rooms-oriented, high-margin, focused-service and compact full-service hotels located within heart of demand locations
As of September 30, 2026, we owned 92 hotel properties with approximately 20,600 rooms

business_model.basis: Revenue types are stated in the 10-Q; the amounts come from the income statement.
business_model.claim: Revenue comes from operating the hotels: room rentals, food and beverage, and other revenue such as parking, amenity fees and gift shop sales. Rooms are the largest line, at 288,366 of 354,476 total revenues in Q3 2026 (table in thousands).
quotes: Our revenues are primarily derived from the operation of hotels, including the sale of rooms, food and beverage revenue and other revenue

business_model.claim: Room revenue was about 81.0% of total revenues in 2025, so room demand and pricing dominate the revenue base.
quotes: Room revenue comprised approximately 81.0% of our total revenues for the year ended December 31, 2025

business_model.claim: The customers are mostly transient business and leisure travelers in major metropolitan business districts. Group business that uses meeting space is a small part of the base.
quotes: As a result of this property profile, the majority of our customers are transient in nature.

business_model.claim: RLJ owns the hotels and leases almost all of them to its taxable REIT subsidiaries (TRSs). Independent third-party managers run the hotels and earn base and incentive fees tied to hotel revenue and profit.
quotes: We lease 91 of the 92 hotel properties to our TRSs

Our hotels are managed by independent, third-party management companies under long-term agreements pursuant to which the management companies typically earn base and incentive management fees based on the levels of revenues and profitability of each individual hotel property.

business_model.claim: Most hotels operate under Marriott, Hilton or Hyatt franchise brands, so results depend on those brand systems. Franchise fees are charged as a percentage of room revenue.
quotes: approximately 89.3% of our hotel properties operating under existing relationships with Marriott, Hilton or Hyatt
A franchise fee is computed as a percentage of room revenue

business_model.basis: Drivers are stated in the 10-K; the Q3 figures are stated in the earnings release.
business_model.claim: Room revenue is driven by occupancy and average daily rate (ADR). In Q3 2026, comparable RevPAR rose 9.7%, with ADR up 6.4% and occupancy up 230 basis points.
quotes: Occupancy and ADR are the major drivers of room revenue.
Comparable RevPAR increased by 9.7% for the three months ended September 30, 2026, driven by ADR growth of 6.4% and a 230 basis point increase in occupancy.

business_model.basis: Amounts are from the income statement; the cost categories are described in the filings.
business_model.claim: The largest cost is hotel property operating expense: room, food and beverage, management and franchise fees, and other operating expenses. It was 238,398 of 324,224 total operating expenses in Q3 2026 (table in thousands).
A rate (ADR) increase raises margins more than an occupancy increase of the same size, because it adds few variable costs.
quotes: Therefore, changes in ADR have a more significant impact on operating margins than changes in Occupancy.

business_model.basis: The figures are stated in the release; the interpretation is partly inferred.
business_model.claim: Operating leverage showed in Q3 2026. Total revenue rose 7.4%, comparable Hotel EBITDA rose 17.5%, and the comparable Hotel EBITDA margin was 26.5%, up 190 basis points.
quotes: allowed us to expand margins and grow Hotel EBITDA at nearly twice the pace of revenues

business_model.basis: Amounts are stated; the interpretation is inferred from the income statement and the debt disclosure.
business_model.claim: Fixed charges absorb much of hotel profit. Q3 2026 depreciation and amortization was 47,723 and interest expense was 29,831 (table in thousands), against net income of 4,576. Debt outstanding was about $2.2 billion.
quotes: $2.2 billion of debt outstanding

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-Q and release; the revenue-base effect is inferred.
business_model.claim: RLJ recycles capital by selling hotels. The 10-Q reports eight hotels sold in two transactions for a combined sales price of approximately $123.2 million. The release reports an October 2026 sale of seven Chicago Midway hotels for $110.0 million.
quotes: The sale of eight hotel properties in two separate transactions for a combined sales price of approximately $123.2 million.

business_model.basis: Requirement stated in the 10-K; cash amounts from the cash flow statement.
business_model.claim: As a REIT, RLJ must distribute 90% of REIT taxable income, so it pays dividends from cash flow and depends on debt or equity capital for large capital projects. It paid common distributions of 68,859 and preferred distributions of 18,836 in the nine months to September 30, 2026 (table in thousands).
quotes: we are required to distribute 90% of our REIT taxable income (excluding net capital gains)

business_model.claim: Revenue is seasonal. Northeastern hotels are weaker from December through March, while Florida hotels are stronger from January through April.
quotes: The lodging industry is seasonal in nature, which can cause quarterly fluctuations in our revenues.

business_model.claim: Management measures hotel performance with non-GAAP measures such as Hotel EBITDA, alongside RevPAR, ADR and occupancy, as well as FFO and Adjusted EBITDA.
quotes: In addition, we use Hotel EBITDA, a non-GAAP financial measure, to assess operating performance.

competitive_position.claim: RLJ describes itself as one of the largest U.S. publicly traded lodging REITs. At year-end 2025 it owned 93 premium-branded focused-service and compact full-service hotels with approximately 20,800 rooms.
quotes: We are one of the largest U.S. publicly-traded lodging REITs in terms of both number of hotels and number of rooms.

competitive_position.claim: The portfolio is affiliated with leading franchisors. About 89.3% of hotels operate under Marriott, Hilton or Hyatt relationships, which the company says gives them loyalty programs, reservation systems and brand recognition.
quotes: Our hotel properties operate under industry-leading, premium brands, with approximately 89.3% of our hotel properties operating under existing relationships with Marriott, Hilton or Hyatt.

competitive_position.claim: Third-quarter 2026 operating performance was strong. Comparable RevPAR was $153.36, up 9.7%, with ADR growth of 6.4% and higher occupancy. Management says this outpaced the industry.

robust RevPAR growth of 9.7%, outpacing the industry, driven by increases in both demand and rate

competitive_position.basis: stated in P2; counter inferred from P6
